A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeltaFlow research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between the appendices and main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original DeltaFlow evaluations on Argoverse 2 and Waymo, cross-domain experiments, runtime measurements and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds nuScenes results and category-level cross-domain results in Tables 3 and 9.

M1.justification: The temporal delta scheme, sparse voxel representation, backbone, decoder and three losses are unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the implementation equations are retained; category-set notation is only clarified.

E1.justification: v2 adds training and evaluation on nuScenes alongside the retained Argoverse 2 and Waymo experiments. This substantially expands dataset coverage to another driving corpus and LiDAR configuration while retaining the scene-flow task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every matched existing experiment. The new nuScenes table uses previously evaluated methods, including SeFlow, FastNSF, NSFP, DeFlow and Flow4D; the additional cross-domain table retains the existing comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 introduces nuScenes preprocessing and evaluation using 10-Hz downsampling, line-fit ground removal and box/velocity-derived flow labels. It adds bucket-normalized cross-domain evaluation excluding Waymo's unlabeled OTHER category. Section 5.4 also specifies target-domain training/optimization for SeFlow and NSFP, qualifying v1's blanket cross-domain description without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: The feature-map analysis from v1 Appendix A is extended in v2 Section 5.5 to inspect final backbone outputs and background suppression. New Appendix B.4 examines generalization by object category. Existing frame-count, temporal-decay and loss ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The additional results follow the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: All seven original tables retain their numerical results. New Table 3 reports nuScenes three-way mean EPE of 2.33 cm for five-frame DeltaFlow versus 3.82 cm for five-frame Flow4D. Table 9 adds category-level transfer results, including DeltaFlow bucket-normalized means of 0.198 and 0.194 in the two transfer directions. These substantially expand reported evidence rather than demonstrate version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(8), the decoder formulation and the Brent-based complexity analysis are retained. The category-set notation adjustment is equivalent; no new proofs or substantive mathematical revisions appear.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the claimed state-of-the-art evaluation scope from Argoverse 2 and Waymo to include nuScenes. The central contributions concerning temporal efficiency, the two proposed losses and cross-domain generalization remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds an interpretation of the backbone output as further suppressing static noise and discusses transfer performance by category. It removes v1's explicit domain-invariance explanation for cross-domain performance. The supervised-label limitation and proposed future self-supervision remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 explains the existing HiMo-based annotation refinement more concretely through velocity-aware bounding-box enlargement and documents nuScenes preprocessing and label construction. Reported hardware, training hyperparameters, architecture details and code/weight access are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations concerning nuScenes, Zenseact, TruckScenes, ground segmentation, zero-shot monocular scene flow and AutoScale. The central positioning against concatenation-based and 4D scene-flow methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of dataset and cross-domain discussions. v1's feature visualization appendix becomes Section 5.5, and its annotation-refinement discussion moves into Section 4.1. Remaining appendices are reorganized, with additional author-contact, conference and acknowledgment edits; most prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3 and 9, redraws and expands the feature-map figure with backbone outputs, and moves the annotation-refinement figure into the main text. Other figures and tables largely retain their displays despite relocation, renumbering and page reflow.

improvement.justification: v1 already provides substantial benchmark and ablation evidence. v2 strengthens validation through nuScenes and category-level transfer results, while clearer annotation-refinement details and expanded feature visualization improve transparency. These gains outweigh a small reporting weakness: Table 9's blanket outperformance claim exceeds what its displayed CAR tie of 0.091 with Flow4D supports.
